method: Static PE disassembly, Ghidra decompilation, recovered Go call graph and argument tracing; no specimen executed. Only the infector decompressor ran in Unicorn with allocator/free stubs and no OS or network access.

evidence: Packer parameters at RVA 0x845c point to original entry RVA 0x2130 and import descriptors RVA 0x32e0. Emulated 0x40728a on all three packed streams: 5154, 1962 and 352 restored bytes, all byte-identical to mapped sections already present.
Original startup 0x401f10 uses GetLogicalDrives and recursively calls 0x401cf0; CFileFind walks paths, excluding WINDOWS/WINNT directories.
0x401ba0 dispatches EXE candidates to 0x401340; four GHO/gho/BAK/bak comparisons converge at 0x401c7b on DeleteFileA. These backups are deletion targets, not an allowlist.
0x401340 copies the current executable through fgetc/fputc into a temporary file, appends host data (optionally byte shifted), writes recovery records, deletes and renames the target.
0x401040 obtains its own short path and COMSPEC, builds /c del plus the path, and invokes ShellExecuteExA. Rename calls elsewhere target infected hosts, not necessarily the module path.
limitations: The large appended host body has no intact infector footer; no ransomware or other family behavior is inferred from the collector filename.

samples.identification: Damaged StormAttack resource-DLL injector and persistence loader
evidence: 0x401150 creates a hidden iexplore/notepad/calc process, allocates remote memory, writes the DLL path, resolves LoadLibraryA and passes it plus the remote buffer to CreateRemoteThread.
0x402460 extracts DLL resource 101 and 0x4023c0 writes the resource bytes to a file.
0x401260 writes the dropped DLL path as REG_EXPAND_SZ ServiceDLL under LanmanServer Parameters.
0x401900 creates an Active Setup GUID key and writes StubPath; it reads, patches and writes a copy of its own image and launches it. Configuration at RVA 0x4120 selects mode 3.
0x401390 builds COMSPEC /c del for its own short path, creates the cleanup child suspended and resumes it.
The .htext section contains long self-move padding and two trampolines, not a separate ransomware payload.
limitations: Resource DLL 101 has 95.4% zero bytes in its mapped image, a completely zero entry at RVA 0x741a and no usable imports or exports. Some outer calls are damaged too. Traits identify retained code profiles, not successful installation, injection or operational DDoS. No Remcos or WannaCry attribution.

samples.identification: Go Ethereum clipboard corrupter with redundant persistence
evidence: main at 0x1400f8060 calls antiSandbox and isDebuggerPresent, requests elevation via PowerShell Start-Process -Verb RunAs when needed, then launches goroutines. Function values at 0x140153960 and 0x140153968 point to createBackupCopies and installPersistence; the third goroutine starts monitorClipboard.

monitorClipboard at 0x1400f7cc0 uses a 500ms ticker, reads clipboard text, skips unchanged text, trims it and tests ^0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40}$. A positive result calls getEncryptedAddress then clipboard.writeAll with the returned string pair.

getEncryptedAddress at 0x1400f6920 Base64-decodes a 60-byte literal and XORs every output byte with 0x55. The actual 45-byte result contains DEL bytes and is not a valid Ethereum address. This is unauthorized clipboard corruption; successful theft is not established.
installRegistryPersistence opens HKCU and HKLM CurrentVersion Run keys with KEY_SET_VALUE and writes its own executable under randomized names, including system-product-like prefixes.

installScheduledTask invokes schtasks /create /tn <randomized> /tr <own executable> /sc hourly /st 00:00 /f. installStartupFolder builds APPDATA/Microsoft/Windows/Start Menu/Programs/Startup and runs a PowerShell WScript.Shell CreateShortcut/TargetPath/Save script.
createBackupCopies writes randomized executable copies into environment-derived directories and invokes attrib to hide them.

antiSandbox measures a requested 100ms sleep and exits if less than 50ms elapsed. isDebuggerPresent checks the native API, environment flags and debugger-name substrings in its own invocation; main sleeps 30s and exits on detection.
limitations: No application C2, miner, ransomware encryption, credential theft or OT interaction was established. Crypto and Windows networking strings include linked Go libraries. No named malware-family attribution is warranted.
